$meta.note: Places NOT already present in src/lib/data/seed/hotspots.ts. Every record carries sources[] and verification. coordinates are null where no authoritative figure was found — do not fabricate them; geocode from the named village/landmark before publishing a map pin.

verification_levels.official: Named on a Government of India / Government of Manipur site (manipurtourism.gov.in, *.nic.in)
verification_levels.corroborated: Two or more independent non-government sources agree
verification_levels.single-source: One source only — confirm before publishing

places.name: Yangkhullen
places.tagline: A Zeme village stacked up a cliff face, built as a fortress
places.description: Yangkhullen clings to the steep slope of the Zi mountain at roughly 1,600 m, its houses stepped up the cliff on stone bastions so that each roof sits at the level of the next doorstep. Around 180 households live here. The village gate carries enormous carved wooden doors showing a warrior with spear and hunting horn standing between the horns of a mithun. It was laid out as a fortress against raiding, and it has stayed largely outside the tourist economy.
places.how_to_reach: 47 km from Maram Centre on the Maram–Peren road. Maram is on NH-2, about 90 km north of Imphal. The final approach is a rough hill road and a walk up into the village — a high-clearance vehicle is effectively required.
tips: Ask permission of the village authority before photographing houses or people — this is a lived-in village, not a site.
There is no formal accommodation; day-trip from Senapati town or Maram.
places.notes: Declared a heritage village of Manipur by the then Chief Minister in 2022; as of the Jan 2026 Sangai Express report the formal heritage-village tag was still awaited.

places.name: Willong Khullen Megaliths
places.tagline: Standing stones no two people ever count the same
places.description: At a clearing the Maram people call Katak Tukhum, on the edge of Willong Khullen village, dozens of megaliths stand upright in no discernible pattern. The tallest reach about seven metres and a metre thick. Local tradition attributes them to the forefathers of the present-day Maram, and the running joke — repeated by everyone who visits — is that you get a different total every time you count them. Unlike Stonehenge there is no circle and no axis; the arrangement is not understood.
places.location: Willong Khullen, Maram–Peren Road, Senapati district
places.how_to_reach: 37 km from NH-2 at Maram, along the Maram–Peren road. Usually combined with Yangkhullen in one trip.
tips: Listed as a State Protected Monument but with no on-site custodian or interpretation — go with a local guide from the village.
Combine with Yangkhullen; both are on the same road out of Maram.
places.notes: Sources differ on stone height — Wikipedia and senapati.nic.in say up to 7 metres; some travel sites say 7 feet. The 7-metre figure is the one on the government page.

places.name: Liyai Khullen
places.tagline: The 500-year-old Poumai village where the Barak river begins
places.description: Liyai Khullen is the largest and oldest Poumai Naga village, reckoned at over 500 years old. The name is glossed locally as 'people of the sea'. The village keeps stone monoliths, old water pools and ancient banyan trees, and the Barak — one of the longest rivers in the region, which eventually reaches the Bay of Bengal — rises here. Caves and waterfalls in the surrounding hills are still being opened up to visitors, including the Vaonuhro valley and a giant Himalayan lily garden.
places.location: Liyai Khullen, Paomata sub-division, Senapati district
places.how_to_reach: 33 km east of Tadubi, which sits on NH-2 roughly 80 km north of Imphal.
tips: The monoliths and sacred pools are living religious sites for the Poumai — ask before entering or photographing.
Caves and the Vaonuhro valley need a village guide; there is no signage.

places.name: Maram Khullen
places.tagline: One of the oldest and largest Naga settlements in the state
places.description: Maram Khullen is among the biggest villages in Senapati district and one of the most studied by anthropologists — a primitive settlement in the technical sense, with an intact traditional village layout, morung houses and stone seats. It is the parent village from which many Maram settlements claim descent.
places.location: Maram Khullen, near Maram on NH-2, Senapati district
places.how_to_reach: Just off NH-2 at Maram, roughly 90 km north of Imphal on the Imphal–Kohima road.
tips: Easy to combine with Willong Khullen and Yangkhullen in a single day out of Senapati town.

places.name: Purul
places.tagline: Where the old games — Toutou and hill wrestling — are still contested
places.description: Purul is the venue for the indigenous games Toutou and traditional wrestling, held during the village's festival season. For a visitor timing a trip around it, it is one of the few places in the valley-to-hills circuit where you can watch a living competitive tradition rather than a staged performance.
places.location: Purul, on NH-39 corridor, Senapati district
places.how_to_reach: 19 km from Maram.
tips: Worth going only around the festival dates — confirm with the Senapati district administration before travelling.

places.name: Koubru Laikha
places.tagline: A riverside Shiva temple that fills on Shivratri
places.description: One of the better-known Shiva temples in Manipur, sitting on the bank of the Imphal river. It is quiet most of the year and packed on Shivratri, when pilgrims come up from the valley.
places.location: Koubru Laikha, off NH-2, Senapati district
places.how_to_reach: On the NH-2 corridor north of Imphal; ask locally at Kanglatongbi for the turning.
tips: Shivratri (Feb/Mar) is the one day it is crowded — and the one day it is most worth seeing.

places.name: Khoupum Valley
places.tagline: Manipur's second-largest valley, and almost nobody goes
places.description: Khoupum is the second-largest valley in Manipur, home to the Rongmei, and holds a large earthen dam, rivers, the Khukdai cave and the Khouduang waterfall — three falls in total. It has become a picnic valley for people who know it, and stays empty otherwise.
places.location: Khoupum Valley, Old Cachar Road, Noney district
places.how_to_reach: 81 km from Imphal on the Old Cachar Road.
tips: Monsoon (June–September) is when the falls are at full volume, but the Old Cachar Road is at its worst then — check road status before setting out.
Carry out your own waste; there is no facility at the falls.

places.name: Kisha Khou
places.tagline: A cliff wall in Tamenglong that hill-trekkers climb for the view
places.description: Kisha Khou is a magnificent cliff face in Tamenglong, listed by the district administration as a trekking destination with local historical importance. It is one of the district's three or four named sites and is almost entirely undeveloped.
places.how_to_reach: From Tamenglong town; arrange a local guide through the district tourism office.
tips: No marked trail or rescue cover — do not attempt without a local guide.

places.name: Zeiladzang Village
places.tagline: Tousem's scenic village, listed by the district and visited by almost no one
places.description: Zeiladzang, in the Tousem sub-division of Tamenglong, is named by the district administration purely for its landscape. There is no tourism infrastructure; the appeal is the village itself and the country around it.
places.how_to_reach: Tousem sub-division, reached from Tamenglong town. Roads are poor; allow a full day.
tips: Arrange the visit through the village authority — there is no visitor facility of any kind.

places.name: Red Hill (Maibam Lokpa Ching)
places.tagline: The closest the Japanese army ever got to Imphal
places.description: A small hillock on the Tiddim Road where Allied and Japanese forces fought from 20 to 29 May 1944 — the southernmost point the Japanese reached in the Battle of Imphal. Japanese veterans built the India Peace Memorial at the foot of the hill; it was inaugurated in 1994 on the battle's 50th anniversary. A cemetery in the foothills holds the tombs of Japanese soldiers, and the Imphal Peace Museum stands at the same foot of the hill.
places.location: Maibam Lokpa Ching, Nambol, Tiddim Road (NH-150), Bishnupur district
places.how_to_reach: Sources give the distance from Imphal as 16 km (Manipur Tourism) and 17 km (Wikipedia) south on Tiddim Road, NH-150. Any Moirang-bound shared vehicle passes it.
tips: Pair it with the Imphal Peace Museum at the same site and the INA Memorial at Moirang, 25 km further down the same road.
Japanese visitors come here on pilgrimage — the memorial is treated as a grave site, not a viewpoint.
places.notes: Distance from Imphal is reported as both 16 km and 17 km. Administratively in Bishnupur district, but TripAdvisor files it under Imphal West.

places.name: Santhei Natural Park, Andro
places.tagline: A lake-and-woodland park on the edge of the potters' village
places.description: A natural park on the edge of Andro, the Meitei pottery village east of Imphal, with a lake, walking paths and picnic ground. It is the most-visited thing in Andro after the pottery itself and the Mutua Bahadur museum, and it is busy with local families at weekends rather than with outside visitors.
places.how_to_reach: Andro village is about 21 km east of Imphal.
places.entry_fee: ₹10 per person; free for children under 10. Parking: ₹20 two-wheeler, ₹30 three-wheeler, ₹50 car, ₹100 heavy four-wheeler.
tips: Go around 7:30 AM — the lake is still and the park is empty.
Combine with the Andro pottery workshops and the Mutua Bahadur museum in the same village.

places.name: Loukoi Pat
places.tagline: A small boating lake on the Tiddim Road most Loktak visitors drive straight past
places.description: A small lake just off the Tiddim Road with boating and a pleasant setting. It sits on the same corridor as Red Hill and Loktak, and is listed by Manipur Tourism among the things to see in and around the lake, but almost every visitor heading for Loktak passes it without stopping.
places.how_to_reach: On NH-150 between Imphal and Moirang, near the Leimaram/Nambol stretch.
tips: Easy 20-minute stop between Red Hill and Loktak — no need to plan a separate trip.

places.name: Nillai Tea Estate
places.tagline: Manipur's organic green-tea garden, hand-plucked and sun-dried
places.description: Nillai Tea Estate sits at Talui, the second-biggest town in Ukhrul district. It specialises in green tea; the leaf is hand-plucked and sun-dried rather than machine-processed. Visitors can walk the gardens, follow the production process, sit for a tasting and birdwatch along the edges.
places.how_to_reach: About 20 km from Ukhrul town; reachable by public transport towards Talui.
tips: April–June and September–October are the pre- and post-monsoon windows when the garden is at its best.
Buy the green tea at the estate — it is hard to find reliably in Imphal.
places.notes: Described in several sources as the first organic tea estate in Manipur — treat that claim as unverified.

places.name: Longpi (Nungbi) Black Pottery Village
places.tagline: Pottery made from crushed serpentine stone, without a wheel
places.description: Longpi black pottery comes from two Tangkhul villages, Longpi Khullen and Longpi Kajui. The body is a paste of ground black serpentine rock and a brown clay found only here; potters shape every piece by hand, with no wheel at all, then polish, sun-dry and fire it in an open bonfire. The black comes from reduction firing and the sheen from rubbing the hot pot with a local tree leaf. The technique is traced back to the Neolithic. Visiting means going to the workshops in the village and watching the whole sequence.
places.location: Longpi Khullen and Longpi Kajui, Ukhrul district
places.how_to_reach: From Ukhrul town by hired vehicle; there is no scheduled service to the workshops.
tips: Buy directly from the potters rather than from Imphal resellers — the price difference goes to the maker.
Longpi ware is genuinely oven- and flame-safe; ask the potter how to season a new pot.

places.name: Kaihlam Caves
places.tagline: Churachandpur's cave system, still largely unmapped
places.description: One of a number of caves in the Churachandpur hills that have yielded historical and cultural material about the communities of the district. Named by Manipur Tourism among the district's destinations; there is no developed access.
places.how_to_reach: From Lamka (Churachandpur town) with a local guide.
tips: Caving here is unsupported — go with people who know the system and carry your own light.
places.notes: Very little published detail exists. Confirm current access and the security situation in Churachandpur before listing this as visitable.

places.name: Bro Waterfall
places.tagline: Chandel's waterfall, on the road to the Myanmar border
places.description: A waterfall in Chandel district, named by Manipur Tourism as one of the district's two headline destinations alongside Moreh. It sits on the corridor running south-east towards the Myanmar border.
places.how_to_reach: From Chandel town on the Imphal–Moreh road (NH-102).
tips: Chandel is a border district — carry photo ID and check current travel advisories.

places.name: Silheipung Garden, Lamlai
places.tagline: A garden on the eastern edge of Imphal, on the Andro road
places.description: A garden at Lamlai on the eastern side of Imphal East, listed by Manipur Tourism among the district's destinations. It is on the same road out to Andro and Nongmaijing hill.
places.how_to_reach: East of Imphal on the Lamlai–Andro road.
tips: Fits into an Andro day trip rather than justifying its own.
places.notes: Only the name and location are published. Confirm timings and entry fee locally before listing.

places.name: Nupi Lal Memorial Complex
places.tagline: The memorial to the two Women's Wars
places.description: The memorial complex in Imphal commemorating the Nupi Lal — the Women's Wars of 1904 and 1939, in which the women of Imphal's markets rose against British colonial policy. It is the counterpart to Ima Keithel a short distance away: the market is where the movement started, this is where it is remembered.
places.how_to_reach: Central Imphal, walkable from Khwairamband Bazar.
tips: 12 December is Nupi Lal Day, when the complex is the focus of a state observance.
Visit after Ima Keithel — the two only make sense together.

places.name: Haolaipai Supao Keikulu Cave, Phuba Thapham
places.tagline: A named cave in a Poumai village few outsiders reach
places.description: A cave at Phuba Thapham in the Paomata sub-division of Senapati, listed by Manipur Tourism under the district's destinations. Phuba Khuman, the neighbouring village, sits 18 km from Paomata and 68 km from Senapati district headquarters, which gives a sense of how far out this is.
places.location: Phuba Thapham, Paomata sub-division, Senapati district
places.how_to_reach: Paomata sub-division, roughly 68 km from Senapati town. Rough hill roads; a local guide is essential.
tips: No infrastructure at all — treat this as an expedition, not a sightseeing stop.

places.name: Takmu Water Sports Complex
places.tagline: Where the boating on Loktak is actually organised
places.description: The water sports complex at Takmu on Loktak, run as the organised boating and watersports point for the lake. It is the official counterpart to the informal boatmen at Thanga and Sendra.
places.how_to_reach: On Loktak near Sendra, about 48 km from Imphal via Moirang.
tips: Confirm operating status before travelling — the complex has been through several operation-and-maintenance tender cycles.

places.name: Ithai Barrage
places.tagline: The dam that turned Loktak into a reservoir
places.description: The Ithai Barrage impounds the Manipur river just below the confluence of the Imphal and Khuga rivers. Built to regulate Loktak's water level for the hydroelectric project, it effectively converted the lake into a reservoir — and is the single most contested piece of infrastructure in Manipur's environmental politics, blamed for the loss of migratory fish and the degradation of the phumdis. For a visitor interested in why Loktak looks the way it does, this is the explanation.
places.how_to_reach: South of Loktak, reachable from Moirang.
tips: Photography around the barrage may be restricted — ask before you shoot.
Read up on the Loktak Protection Act controversy first; the site means little without the argument around it.

places.name: Ango Ching
places.tagline: An Ukhrul hill on the official list and almost nowhere else
places.description: A hill in Ukhrul district named by Manipur Tourism among the district's destinations, alongside Shirui and the Khangkhui caves. Published detail is minimal.
places.how_to_reach: From Ukhrul town; ask at the district tourism office.
tips: Confirm access locally — this is a name on a list rather than a developed site.
places.notes: Listed officially but with no description anywhere. Verify on the ground before publishing as a visitable destination.

places.name: Chingkhei Ching
places.tagline: The reserved forest ridge on Imphal's eastern skyline
places.description: Chingkhei Ching is a reserved forest on the eastern edge of Imphal, adjoining the larger Nongmaiching reserved forest. It is a walking and birding ridge rather than a built attraction, and it has been repeatedly damaged by deliberate fires — a Joint Forest Management Committee issue reported in the local press.
places.location: Chingkhei Ching reserved forest, Imphal East district
places.how_to_reach: Eastern edge of Imphal, adjoining the Nongmaiching range.
tips: Go early for birds; the ridge is exposed and hot by mid-morning.

places.name: Kachouphung Lake
places.tagline: A hill lake in Kamjong with a second, smaller lake beside it
places.description: Kachouphung is a lake in the Ukhrul–Kamjong belt, listed by Manipur Tourism together with the nearby Azoa Jenephiu Magi lake and a cold water fishery project. It is one of the eastern hills' quietest water bodies.
places.how_to_reach: From Ukhrul town towards Kamjong; hired vehicle required.
tips: Kamjong borders Myanmar — carry photo ID and check advisories.
places.notes: Already present in the existing hotspot seed as 'kachouphung-lake' — merge rather than duplicate. Added here only for the Azoa Jenephiu Magi lake and cold-water fishery detail.

unresolved_conflicts.detail: manipurtourism.gov.in/escape-to-the-hills places Sadu Chiru in the Sadar Hills, 20 km from Imphal beside Tiddim Road (NH-150), and calls it newly opened. senapati.nic.in places Sadu Chiru at Sadu near Ichum Keirap, 27 km from Imphal, with a 30 m first fall and an adjacent Agape park. Several travel sites treat 'Sadu Chiru' and 'Leimaram Falls' as the same three-tiered site, while Leimaram is in Bishnupur district. These may be two distinct waterfalls conflated in secondary sources.
unresolved_conflicts.action: Verify on the ground before publishing distance, district or a merged record.

unresolved_conflicts.detail: The Keibul Homestay host is given as 'Ashok Samapcha' on homestaysofindia.com and as 'Ashok Sapamcha' on manipurtourism.gov.in (Loktak Aquamarine Homestay). 'Sapam' is the common Meitei surname, so 'Sapamcha' is likely correct. It is also unclear whether Keibul Homestay and Loktak Aquamarine Homestay are the same operation under two names.
unresolved_conflicts.action: Call +91 80149 21286 to confirm the name and whether the two listings are one business.
